name: Question 11
problem:
Consider the inexact differential equation

$$
(\frac{5{y}^{2}}{x}+2{y}^{3})\,\text{d}x+(5y+2x{y}^{2}+\frac{2}{{x}^{2}})\,\text{d}y=0.
$$

It is known that 

$$
\frac{1}{Q}(\frac{∂P}{∂y}-\frac{∂Q}{∂x})=\frac{2}{x}
$$

where the functions $P$ and $Q$ are given by 

$$
P(x,y)=\frac{5{y}^{2}}{x}+2{y}^{3},\,Q(x,y)=5y+2x{y}^{2}+\frac{2}{{x}^{2}}.
$$

Use this information to find a suitable integrating factor $I(x)$ and hence find the general solution to the equation.$\,$ A suitable integrating factor is $I(x)=$ {{field-1}}.

$\,$ The general solution is {{field-2}}, where $c$ is a constant.

Consider the inexact differential equation (5y2x+2y3)dx+(5y+2xy2+2x2)dy=0. It is known that 1Q(∂P∂y−∂Q∂x)=2x where the functions P and Q are given by P(x,y)=5y2x+2y3,Q(x,y)=5y+2xy2+2x2. Use this information to find a suitable integrating factor I(x) and hence find the general solution to the equation. A suitable integrating factor is I(x)=
 
e2x
x2
1x2
x3
.

The general solution is
 
52x2y2+13x3y3+2y=c
2x2y2+23x3y3+y=c
x2y2+x3y3+y=c
52x2y2+23x3y3+2y=c
, where c is a constant.
